title: Boundless space: the first formless state
hookLine: an emptied room looks bigger; the manual's first formless state lets the object go and attends to the space
carry: boundless space: what's left when the image goes
tomorrow: and what is it that knows all that space?

cards: A room looks bigger once the furniture's carried out. Same walls, same floor, and somehow more room than before. The Visuddhimagga's answer to yesterday's question works a little like that.
Remember the colored discs from a few weeks back, the kasinas? A meditator spreads the image of the disc in the mind until it's vast, and then lets it go. What's left is what it was sitting in.

teach.b: This is the first of the formless states, the base of boundless space. The manual is clear that it's for someone with deep concentration, who has already reached the fourth jhana with a kasina.
For everyone else, it's a picture worth having. The method begins with a reason.
Anything with form, the manual says, brings trouble with it: sticks and knives, quarrels, sickness in the eyes and ears.
So the meditator stops attending to the image and attends to the space it filled, saying inwardly: space, space. Boundless space.

teach.h: SET IT DOWN, NOTICE THE ROOM.
teach.b: Notice the move. Nothing new is added. Something is let go of, and room appears that was there all along.
That's the part anyone can borrow on a cramped week. When one thing fills the whole view, a grade, a message, a no, the practice isn't to fight it or polish it.
It's to set it down for a moment and notice the room around it.

how: In Theravada meditation manuals the base of boundless space is the first of four formless attainments, practiced by meditators with deep concentration after the fourth jhana; teachers present it to beginners as a description rather than an instruction.

o: clearing every object out of your bedroom
picturing yourself floating through the stars
attending to endless space once the object is gone

games.q: from disc to space — tap the pairs.
p: the disc the meditator starts from

s: boundless space means imagining you're floating in outer space
it's attending to the space a meditation image filled, once the image is let go.
the manual presents this state for meditators with deep concentration
it follows the fourth jhana; for most people it's a picture worth having.

games.q: your sister gets one bad grade and says her whole year is ruined. what's the boundless-space move?
o: help her stare at the grade until every mistake is found.
let the grade be set down a moment, and notice what's around it.
tell her it doesn't matter and to forget it ever happened.
games.why: nothing is added and nothing is denied: the one thing filling the view is set down, and the room that was there all along shows up.

practice: Look out a window, or up at the ceiling if there isn't one, and let your eyes rest not on any thing but on the space between things.
Then let the sense of that space widen past the walls, a sky with no edge, and whenever a thing grabs your attention, let it go and come back to the room around it.

wordCard.voice: Boundless space: the first formless state. The image is let go, and only endless space is attended to.

orig.note: Pali: akasa, space, with anancayatana, the base of endlessness: the base of boundless space.

carryVoice: The line to keep: boundless space, what's left when the image is let go, the room that was there all along. Day thirty-three of forty.

sources.ref: Visuddhimagga 10 (the base consisting of boundless space: one with the fourth jhana sees the danger in materiality, removes the kasina, and attends to the space as 'space, space' / 'infinite space')
